title: Why 1×1 Convolutions Save Compute
tagline: Compare a direct 3x3 conv with a 1x1 bottleneck and watch the FLOP bars diverge several-fold
summary: Two paths produce the same output shape: a direct 3x3 convolution, or a 1x1 projection to a narrow C_mid followed by the 3x3. Sliders for C_in, C_mid, C_out, and spatial size drive a live FLOP comparison drawn as two bars to scale, with the bottleneck split into its 1x1 and 3x3 pieces and a savings ratio called out. A ResNet-style preset shows the several-fold win; pushing C_mid past C_in shows the ratio drop below one, making crisp when the bottleneck actually pays.
highlights: See the multiply-add cost of a direct 3x3 conv versus a 1x1 bottleneck as two bars drawn to scale.
The bottleneck bar is split into its cheap 1x1 projection and its 3x3 on the narrowed channel stack.
A live savings ratio shows the several-fold win of a ResNet-style bottleneck.
Push C_mid past C_in and watch the ratio fall below one, so the bottleneck only pays when the waist is narrow.
The exact formula 9 C_in C_out over C_mid (C_in + 9 C_out) is rendered with your current numbers plugged in.
